description: SaaS and online service subscription cancellations. Primarily governed by federal law (FTC, ROSCA) and state auto-renewal laws.
typical_barriers: Annual lock-in with no pro-rata refund
Claims data will be lost upon cancellation
Charges for unused months after cancellation

email_1.subject: Cancellation of Subscription — {{company_name}} — Account: {{account_identifier}}
key_points: Clear cancellation request with account email/ID
If auto-renewed without proper notice, cite applicable law
If annual plan auto-renewed, request prorated refund
Request confirmation that no further charges will be made
saas_specific_points: If auto-renewal was not clearly disclosed, services may be deemed an 'unconditional gift' under CA ARL §17603
Request data portability / export before cancellation takes effect
If enterprise/business plan, check if different terms apply

email_2.subject: Follow-Up: Subscription Cancellation — SECOND REQUEST
key_points: Mention credit card dispute for post-cancellation charges

email_3.subject: Final Notice: Subscription Cancellation — {{company_name}}
key_points: State intent to file FTC complaint
State intent to file state AG complaint
For CA: cite unconditional gift provision if auto-renewal non-compliant

notes: SaaS cancellations are often straightforward but some companies make it deliberately difficult. The strongest argument is usually that auto-renewal was not properly disclosed per state law (CA ARL is especially strong with the 'unconditional gift' provision). Annual plans that auto-renewed are common — check if renewal notice was sent in advance.
